definition: ASP.NET Core Web API is a core concept in .NET Full Stack. It refers to the techniques, principles and practices that let a practitioner work effectively with this topic in real systems.

theory.heading: What ASP.NET Core Web API is
theory.body: ASP.NET Core Web API describes the methods and patterns used within .NET Full Stack to achieve reliable, maintainable results. Understanding it is the foundation for everything built later in this course.
points: ASP.NET Core Web API is a named, repeatable concept.
It has a clear purpose and scope.
It connects to other course topics.

theory.heading: Why ASP.NET Core Web API matters
theory.body: Without ASP.NET Core Web API, systems built with .NET Full Stack are harder to debug, extend and operate. Teams that master this topic ship fewer defects and communicate more clearly about design decisions.

theory.heading: How ASP.NET Core Web API works
theory.body: The mechanism behind ASP.NET Core Web API follows a repeatable sequence: understand the requirement, apply the principle, verify the result and refine based on feedback. Each step has checks that keep the work on track.
points: Apply the core principle of ASP.NET Core Web API.

theory.heading: Advantages and limitations of ASP.NET Core Web API
theory.body: ASP.NET Core Web API offers structure, clarity and consistency, but it also adds overhead and may be overkill for trivial tasks. Use it when the benefit in reliability outweighs the added effort.
points: Limitations: added overhead, not always needed.
